title: Congress party workers protest against playwright in Bengaluru

tea.why: Congress party workers protested against playwright Addanda C. Cariappa over his play regarding Mahatma Gandhi's assassination.
tea.want: Protesters demanded the arrest of the playwright, the cancellation of his play, and legal action against him.
tea.changed: Nov 2: Congress workers staged a protest at the police commissioner's office and confronted the playwright outside the venue.

summary: Bengaluru Congress party workers staged a protest at the Bengaluru City Police Commissioner's office on November 2, 2026, demanding the arrest of playwright Addanda C. Cariappa. According to the sources, the protest followed allegations that his play on Mahatma Gandhi's assassination contained derogatory remarks and attempted to portray Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and Nathuram Godse as figures who secured India's independence. Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee leaders submitted a memorandum to the police seeking action against the playwright and the cancellation of the drama. During continued demonstrations outside the Suchitra Cinema and Cultural Academy in Banashankari, protesters confronted Cariappa, and an unidentified person hurled a shoe at him amid a heavy police presence. Authorities deployed Karnataka State Reserve Police platoons and local police for security, while police filed an FIR over an earlier ink-smearing incident and an NCR regarding Monday's events.
demands: Cancel the staging of the play
Take legal action against the playwright
response: Police deployed two platoons of the Karnataka State Reserve Police alongside jurisdictional officers for security at the venue. Authorities stated an FIR was registered regarding an earlier ink-smearing incident and an NCR was filed over Monday's confrontation.

updates.text: Congress party workers staged a protest at the Bengaluru City Police Commissioner's office demanding the playwright's arrest.
A shoe was hurled at the playwright outside the Suchitra Cinema and Cultural Academy amid demonstrations.
